items.question: Which tag holds everything the visitor sees on the page?
items.explanation: The <body> element holds the visible content. The <head> holds information about the page, such as its title.
items.hint: The visible part of the page.

items.question: Type the missing tag name so this becomes the most important heading on the page.
items.explanation: <h1> is the top-level heading. Use only one per page.
items.hint: Headings go from h1 to h6.

items.question: Which tag marks text as very important (shown bold by default)?
items.explanation: <strong> means very important. <em> means emphasized and is shown in italics.

items.question: Type the attribute that holds the address of a link.
items.explanation: href stands for hypertext reference. It is the address the link goes to.

items.question: Which attribute gives an image a text description for screen readers?
items.explanation: alt is the alternative text. It is read aloud and is shown if the image cannot load.

items.question: Which tag creates a numbered list?
items.explanation: <ol> is an ordered (numbered) list. <ul> is an unordered (bulleted) list. <li> is each item inside either.

items.question: Type the tag name that makes one row of a table.
items.explanation: <tr> means table row. Inside it, <td> makes data cells and <th> makes heading cells.

items.question: Which tag creates a heading cell inside a table?
items.explanation: <th> is a table heading cell, bold and centered by default. <td> is a normal data cell.

items.question: Type the input type that hides the characters while the user types.
items.explanation: type="password" shows dots instead of the letters.

items.question: A label has for="email". What must the matching input have?
items.explanation: The label's for attribute must match the input's id. Then clicking the label selects the field.

items.question: Which tag is best for the main group of navigation links?
items.explanation: <nav> tells browsers and screen readers that this is a navigation area. <div> has no meaning.

items.question: Write the HTML for a bulleted list with two items: Rice and Eggs.
items.explanation: A bulleted list uses <ul>, and each item is wrapped in <li>.
